definitions.explanation: relating to or depending on a specific individual rather than a system, role, or territory

examples.japanese: この{業務|ぎょうむ}は{属人|ぞくじん}{的|てき}になっている。
examples.english: This task has become dependent on a specific individual.

examples.japanese: {属人|ぞくじん}{的|てき}な{仕事|しごと}の{やり方|やりかた}を{見直|みなお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: We need to reconsider our person-dependent way of working.

examples.japanese: {知識|ちしき}が{特定|とくてい}の{社員|しゃいん}に{属人|ぞくじん}{化|か}すると、その{人|ひと}が{辞|や}めたときに{会社|かいしゃ}が{困|こま}る。
examples.english: When knowledge becomes concentrated in specific employees, the company suffers if those people leave.

notes:
A formal term meaning "belonging to or dependent on a specific person." In business contexts, {属人|ぞくじん}{化|か} (becoming person-dependent) is considered a problem — when only one person knows how to do something, their absence creates risk. The opposite concept is {属地|ぞくち} (territory-based) in legal contexts, or マニュアル{化|か}/システム{化|か} (systematization) in business.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {属人|ぞくじん}{的|てき}: person-dependent (adjective)
- {属人|ぞくじん}{化|か}: becoming person-dependent
- {属人|ぞくじん}{化|か}を{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent person-dependency
- {属人|ぞくじん}{主義|しゅぎ}: personalism (in law: the principle of personal jurisdiction)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {属地|ぞくち}: territory-based — the legal counterpart: based on location rather than person
- {個人|こじん}{的|てき}: personal/individual — more general, without the negative connotation of dependency
